hints: Look closely at what changed and what did not after 24 hours: P went down, but Q stayed exactly the same.
Remember the two key features of an enzyme reaction: the substrate gets used up, while the enzyme (biological catalyst) is unchanged at the end.
walkthrough:
**Observe the results**

Think like a detective. After mixing P and Q for 24 hours, P decreased but Q did not change.

That tells us P is being lost or changed, while Q is not being used up.

**Apply the enzyme idea**

A biological catalyst is an enzyme. Enzymes speed up the breakdown of a substrate, but they are not used up themselves.

This fits perfectly: if Q is the enzyme and P is the substrate, we would expect P to fall and Q to stay constant.

**Notice the careful word may**

The conclusions all say may. We have no control tube with P alone, so P could also just break down naturally over time.

Because we cannot rule it out, conclusion 1 is also possible, so 1, 2 and 3 are all supported.

options.A: All three are possible. P falling fits natural breakdown (1), and also fits Q acting as unchanged enzyme (2) on P as substrate (3).
options.B: This misses out 3. If Q is the catalyst, then P which is decreasing is very likely its substrate.
options.C: This is too limited. The unchanged Q strongly suggests enzyme action, so 2 and 3 are also supported.
options.D: This misses out 1. Without a control of P alone, we cannot rule out that P simply breaks down over time.
